correctness.rationale: For X=[[c,a],[b,-c]], direct multiplication gives X²=(c²+ab)I, hence X^P=Q^((P-1)/2)X for P odd. Partition triples by common t-adic order v. For primitive length r=m-v, the smooth nonzero cone c²+ab=0 mod t has q²−1 points and exactly q² lifts per new precision, so number satisfying Q=0 mod t^h is (q²−1)q^(3r-h-2). For Pv>=m count ideal t^ceil(m/P) triples; otherwise h_v=ceil(2(m-Pv)/(P-1)) gives exact kernel count. Reduction mod t identifies nilpotents and total q^(3m-1). Primitive Q=t witnesses maximal height, and geometric bounds on low-P kernel fraction establish concentration at logarithmic scale. Original finite source enumerates six small prime truncations; separate independent checks enumerated q=3,m<=3 and q=5,m<=2; no finite proof of all q,m.
